# supervise

```go
import "github.com/lucasavila00/immutago/pkg/supervise"
```

Package supervise runs services with owned child lifetimes and terminal failures.

Embed Service\[A\], supply Run\(context.Context\), and optionally declare Init\(\) error. Start initializes the service and returns Ref\[T\]. Calls through Borrow run in the caller's goroutine; review shared fields, locks, and inputs in service code. A Run failure stops the root. Groups control lifetime and stop order.

## type Failure

Failure describes one service Run panic or runtime.Goexit call. The root panics with the first recorded \*Failure after reporting and cleanup. Value is the original panic value, or an error with the text "supervise: service called runtime.Goexit" for Goexit. Stack is captured in that service's goroutine. Groups pass the same failure to the root without wrapping it.

```go
type Failure struct {
    Service string
    Value   any
    Stack   []byte
}
```

### func \(\*Failure\) Error

```go
func (f *Failure) Error() string
```

Error names the service and its terminal failure.

### func \(\*Failure\) Unwrap

```go
func (f *Failure) Unwrap() error
```

Unwrap returns the original failure when it is an error.

## type Group

Group owns an ordered set of service lifetimes and nested groups. It activates at most once and stops at most once. The zero value is not usable. Do not copy an initialized Group. Pass its pointer. Run go vet to check for copies.

```go
type Group struct {
    // contains filtered or unexported fields
}
```

### func NewRoot

```go
func NewRoot(report func(any, []byte)) *Group
```

NewRoot creates an active lifetime group. A Run panic or Goexit stops the root, waits for ordered cleanup, and panics with \*Failure. report receives each recovered Run panic or Goexit once as \*Failure, with its original stack, before that service waits for child cleanup. A nil report writes failures to standard error. Stop does not suppress failures. Reports can overlap, must return, and must not wait for their group to stop.

### func StartGroup

```go
func StartGroup(parent *Group) *Group
```

StartGroup creates a lifetime group for selective shutdown. A Run failure in any child stops the root. A stopped parent returns a stopped group.

### func \(\*Group\) Stop

```go
func (s *Group) Stop() <-chan struct{}
```

Stop closes admission in the subtree and requests ordered shutdown. It returns the same completion channel on every call. Shutdown waits for children in reverse start order, then removes a nested group from its parent. It does not wait for ordinary direct method calls. A service can request its group's stop, but must not wait for that group from its own Run.

## type NoArgs

NoArgs supplies empty start arguments.

type NoArgs struct{}

## type Ref

Ref holds an initialized service value. Copies select the same value. Stop does not invalidate a reference or wait for direct service method calls.

```go
type Ref[T any] struct {
    im.Frozen
    // contains filtered or unexported fields
}
```

### func Start

```go
func Start[T, A any, P interface {
    *T
    Init() error
    Run(context.Context)
    bind(A, *Group)
    begin(context.Context) (context.Context, bool)
    halt()
    end()
}](parent *Group, args A) (Ref[T], error)
```

Start creates T, calls Init once in the caller, and publishes the initialized value. An Init error returns a zero Ref and the error; an Init panic reaches the caller. The runtime stops staged children in both cases. Each successful Init gets one Run call, with a cancelled context if the service cannot activate. Start under a stopped parent waits for that cleanup Run. Stop waits for registered children, not an Init that has not registered yet.

### func \(Ref\[T\]\) Borrow

```go
func (p Ref[T]) Borrow() *T
```

Borrow returns the initialized service value, including after Stop. The pointer can be stored and reused. Calls use ordinary Go synchronization. A zero reference panics with "supervise: zero Ref".

### func \(Ref\[T\]\) IsZero

```go
func (p Ref[T]) IsZero() bool
```

IsZero reports whether this reference is unset.

## type Service

Service supplies start arguments and the children owned by this service. Embed it by value. Start creates and initializes the service value. Do not copy an initialized Service or a struct that contains it. Declare service methods with pointer receivers. Run go vet to check for copies.

```go
type Service[A any] struct {
    // contains filtered or unexported fields
}
```

### func \(\*Service\[A\]\) Args

```go
func (p *Service[A]) Args() A
```

Args returns the arguments supplied to Start.

### func \(\*Service\[A\]\) Init

```go
func (*Service[A]) Init() error
```

Init supplies empty setup when the service does not declare Init. A declared Init must release application resources if it fails. The runtime stops children created by that setup.

### func \(\*Service\[A\]\) UncheckedChildren

```go
func (p *Service[A]) UncheckedChildren() *Group
```

UncheckedChildren returns the child group owned by this service. Call it on the original service pointer created by Start, never a value copy. Parent shutdown stops and waits for the children. After the parent ends, UncheckedChildren returns a stopped group.
